question:
In the figure below, semicircles with centers at \(A\) and \(B\) and with radii \(2\) and \(1,\) respectively, are drawn in the interior of, and sharing bases with, a semicircle with diameter \(\overline{JK}.\) The two smaller semicircles are externally tangent to each other and internally tangent to the largest semicircle. A circle centered at \(P\) is drawn externally tangent to the two smaller semicircles and internally tangent to the largest semicircle. What is the radius of the circle centered at \(P?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2017_AMC_12A_Q16_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Tangency gives useful distances between centers: externally tangent circles have center distance equal to the sum of their radii, while internally tangent circles have center distance equal to their radius difference.

Let \(O\) be the center of the largest semicircle. The smaller diameters lie along \(JK\). Internal tangency places their outer endpoints at \(J\) and \(K\), and external tangency makes their diameters meet without a gap. Thus
\[
JK=2(2)+2(1)=6,
\]
so the largest radius is \(3\). Choose coordinates
\[
J=(0,0),\quad A=(2,0),\quad O=(3,0),\quad B=(5,0).
\]
Let the desired radius be \(r\), where \(0<r<3\), and write \(P=(x,y)\), with \(y>0\). The three tangencies give
\[
PA=r+2,\qquad PB=r+1,\qquad PO=3-r.
\]
Using the distance formula,
\[
\begin{aligned}
(x-2)^2+y^2&=(r+2)^2,\\
(x-5)^2+y^2&=(r+1)^2,\\
(x-3)^2+y^2&=(3-r)^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
All three equations contain the same \(y^2\). Subtracting the third equation from each of the first two also cancels the \(x^2\) and \(r^2\) terms, leaving
\[
2x-5=10r-5
\]
and
\[
-4x+16=8r-8.
\]
These simplify to \(x=5r\) and \(x=6-2r\). Therefore
\[
5r=6-2r,\qquad 7r=6,\qquad r=\frac67.
\]
To check the original geometry, this value gives \(x=30/7\), and the third distance equation gives
\[
y^2=\left(\frac{15}{7}\right)^2-\left(\frac97\right)^2=\frac{144}{49}.
\]
Taking the positive height gives \(P=(30/7,12/7)\). Its distances to \(A,B,O\) are respectively \(20/7,13/7,15/7\), exactly \(r+2,r+1,3-r\). Also \(12/7>r\), so the circle lies above the diameter. Thus the required radius is \(\boxed{\frac67}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
